findings.evidence: Lines 84–87 prove `powEnd z f = f ^ z`, but subsequent proofs must explicitly use `[powEnd_apply]`; lines 121–124 and 157–162 likewise state direct application normal forms without annotations.
findings.fix: Mark these application/characteristic lemmas `@[simp]` so their custom operations reduce to powers or scalar multiplication.
findings.issue: The principal elimination theorem `powEnd_apply` lacks `@[simp]`, so applications of the opaque `powEnd` do not normalize to the advertised power map; the same omission affects `toAdditive_powEnd_apply` at line 121 and `charPoints_cocharPoints_apply` at line 157.

findings.evidence: Lines 128–130 orient `(z : AddMonoid.End …) = MonoidHom.toAdditive (powEnd … z)`, expanding a standard cast into the newly defined representation.
findings.fix: Reverse the theorem to `MonoidHom.toAdditive (powEnd … z) = (z : AddMonoid.End …)` and mark that orientation `@[simp]`, or remove `@[simp]` from the current orientation.
findings.issue: `@[simp] intCast_eq_toAdditive_powEnd` rewrites the canonical integer cast into the more specialized opaque `toAdditive (powEnd z)`, which is the wrong normal-form direction.

summary: The characteristic application API does not simplify automatically, while the integer-cast bridge is oriented away from the canonical normal form.
